🚀 Remote Deployment Console — Administrator & Visual User Guide

Version 1.4.0.14 • 64-Bit Signed Windows WPF Console (ps_deploy.exe / ps_deploy.ps1)

A comprehensive, step-by-step visual guide for Windows System Administrators to configure credentials, synchronize Active Directory Organizational Units (OUs), auto-probe computer inventory, build multi-step silent installation packages (.bat, .msi, .exe, .ps1, Office Click-to-Run XML), and monitor parallel remote deployments in real time.

1. Application Overview & Workspace Layout

Remote Deployment Console (PSDeploy) is a single-window, dark-themed (Catppuccin Mocha) Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) console engineered for parallel software deployment, remote scripting, and real-time computer inventory monitoring across Active Directory domains.

Key Workspace Regions (Resizable with Persistent Splitters)

Workspace Region Location Primary Capabilities
Top Header Bar Top Banner Displays 🚀 Remote Deployment Console with Version 1.4.0.14 directly below the title, live authentication/staging summary, and the ⚙️ Settings button.
📚 Package Library Left Column Hierarchical folder tree of saved deployment packages. Supports drag-and-drop between folders, right-click context menus, JSON import/export, and double-click to edit steps.
🎯 Computer Inventory Upper-Right Panel Target computers synced from Active Directory OUs or added manually/via CSV, background batched auto-probing (ICMP + DNS + C$/WinRM + Active Logon User), and live 🟢 Online / 🔴 Offline counters.
🚀 Deployment Middle-Right Panel Displays the currently selected package badge, 🚀 Deploy Selected Package button, and the live Running Deployments & Deployment History table.
📊 Status Log Bottom Panel Per-computer execution status, per-column Excel-style sorting/filtering, 💾 Export to CSV, and double-click drill-down into real-time Step Output & Diagnostic Details.

2. Top Header Bar, Version Badge & Global Settings (⚙️ Settings)

Directly below the 🚀 Remote Deployment Console title in the top-left header bar, the console displays the active build version (Version 1.4.0.14) synchronized automatically by build_exe.ps1. To the right of the title, the live summary bar displays your active authentication mode, local configuration path, remote staging folder, concurrency level, and auto-probe interval.

Configuring Credentials, Staging & Auto-Probing

Click ⚙️ Settings in the top-right corner to open the PSDeploy Settings dialog:

  • 🔑 WinRM Deployment Credentials:
    • Check Use my current Windows logon credentials to authenticate using your current interactive Kerberos/NTLM session, or uncheck it to specify a dedicated Domain (e.g., NMFS.LOCAL), Username, and Password.
    • Saved passwords are encrypted on disk using Windows DPAPI (DataProtectionScope::CurrentUser) inside settings.json and can only be decrypted by your Windows user account on the console machine.
    • Localhost & Remote Elevation: When deploying to either a remote computer or the local machine (localhost), PSDeploy automatically uses your saved admin credential and registers an isolated Session 0 SYSTEM Scheduled Task so installers never trigger interactive UAC prompts or stall waiting for hidden UI windows.
  • 💾 Application Configuration & Library Directory: Choose where settings.json, package_library.json, ad_sync_config.json, and layout_state.json are stored.
  • 📁 Remote Machine Staging Directory: Default is C:\Temp\PSDeploy. During deployment, step payloads are copied into C:\Temp\PSDeploy\Step_<N> on the target computer.
  • ⚡ Concurrent Deployment: Configure between 1 (Sequential) and 8 Hosts (Max) simultaneous target deployments via background RunspacePool threads.
  • 🔍 Computer Inventory Auto-Probing: Enable automatic non-blocking background probing on startup and every 5, 10, 15, 30, or 60 minutes.

3. Package Library Management (📚 PACKAGE LIBRARY)

The left-hand Package Library panel organizes all reusable deployment packages into folders (e.g., Software, Microsoft Office, Scripts, Maintenance).

  • + New — Opens the Package Steps Builder modal with a blank package ready to configure.
  • 📁 Folder — Creates a new category folder in the Package Library tree.
  • 🗑 Delete — Deletes the selected package or empty folder from the library.
  • Single-Click a Package: Loads the package as the Active Package in the Deployment panel so it can be deployed immediately.
  • Double-Click a Package (or Right-Click → Edit Package Steps...): Opens the Package Steps Builder modal to add, reorder, or modify steps.
  • Drag-and-Drop: Drag any package node onto another folder header to move it between folders.
  • Right-Click Context Menu: Supports Edit Package Steps..., New Folder..., Save Active Package Here, Rename... (F2), Import Packages (.json)..., and Export Package(s) (.json)....

4. Package Steps Builder & Step Types

Double-clicking a package in the library (or clicking + New) opens the Package Steps Builder modal window. Steps execute sequentially (Step 1, Step 2, Step 3...) on each target machine.

Supported Step Types

Toolbar Button Step Type Execution Behavior & Options
📦 Install Installer Stages and executes .bat, .cmd, .msi, .exe, .msp, .msu, or .ps1 installers. Supports Include Entire Directory, Additional Files / Folders, Clean up temp directory after install, and custom Success Codes (default: 0,1641,3010,2359302,17003).
⌨ Command Command / Batch Runs inline Windows Batch/CMD commands via cmd.exe /c on the target computer, with optional companion files staged into the step working directory.
⚡ PowerShell PowerShell Script Executes inline or file-based PowerShell scripts with configurable ErrorActionPreference, custom success exit codes, and optional companion files.
📁 File Copy File / Folder Copy Copies a single file, multiple files, or an entire directory tree to a specified target folder on the remote machine (with overwrite and subfolder creation toggles).
🔄 Reboot Reboot / Shutdown Reboots or shuts down the target computer with configurable countdown timer (seconds), custom broadcast message, and optional wait-for-host-online recovery check.
⏱ Sleep Sleep / Pause Pauses package execution for a configurable number of seconds (1–3600s) between steps.
💬 Message Popup Message Sends an interactive popup message via msg.exe to active logged-on user sessions on the target computer.
🚪 Logoff Logoff Users Gracefully or forcibly logs off active interactive user sessions on the target machine before or after maintenance steps.
📚 Canned-Scripts Built-In Script Catalog One-click library of pre-built SysAdmin scripts (BitLocker status, GPUpdate, DNS/Winsock reset, Windows Update check, Disk cleanup, Service health, Installed software audit).

5. Configuring Installer Steps (.bat, .msi, .exe & Office Click-to-Run XML)

The Edit Step — Install (.bat / .msi / .exe / .ps1) dialog supports both full-directory staging (such as a multi-gigabyte Microsoft Office 365 offline installation folder) and targeted companion file staging (such as setup.exe + RemoveAll.xml).

Scenario A: Full Directory Staging (e.g., Office M365 Offline Install via .bat or setup.exe)

When deploying a package that requires all subfolders and payload files in the installer directory (such as M365_install.bat calling setup.exe /configure NWC_M365_Config.xml alongside the Office\Data cabinet folder):

  1. Select your Install File (e.g., C:\Downs\M365\M365_install.bat or setup.exe).
  2. Check ☑️ Include Entire Directory. The dialog automatically calculates and displays the total file count and size (e.g., Entire Directory: 20 Files 3.5 GB).
  3. Check ☑️ Clean up temp directory after install if you want PSDeploy to automatically delete the staged 3.5 GB folder from C:\Temp\PSDeploy\Step_1 once installation finishes.

Scenario B: Targeted Companion Files (e.g., Uninstall MS Office with setup.exe + RemoveAll.xml)

When you only need the primary executable plus one or two configuration files (without copying a 3.5 GB Data folder):

  1. Select C:\Downs\M365\setup.exe as the Install File.
  2. Enter /configure RemoveAll.xml in the Parameters box.
  3. Leave Include Entire Directory unchecked, and click + Files... next to Additional Files to add C:\Downs\M365\RemoveAll.xml.
  4. Check ☑️ Clean up temp directory after install and click OK.
💡 Office Click-to-Run Exit Code 17003 Handled Automatically:
When setup.exe /configure RemoveAll.xml removes Microsoft 365 / Office Click-to-Run, Microsoft's bootstrapper frequently returns exit code 17003 while ClickToRunSvc finalizes product removal. PSDeploy v1.4.0.14 includes 17003 in its default Installer Success Codes (0,1641,3010,2359302,17003) and automatically waits for any lingering child OfficeClickToRun.exe removal processes to finish before cleaning up the staging directory and reporting Success.

6. Computer Inventory, Active Directory Sync & Background Probing

The 🎯 COMPUTER INVENTORY panel maintains your persistent list of target workstations and servers across application restarts, tracks real-time 🟢 Online and 🔴 Offline counts on the bottom status bar, and resolves the active Current Logon User.

Synchronizing Organizational Units (OUs) from Active Directory (🔄 Sync AD)

  1. Click 🔄 Sync AD in the Computer Inventory toolbar to open the Active Directory Sync & Schedule Configuration dialog.
  2. Click + Include OUs... to open the hierarchical Include Active Directory Containers tree browser, enter your domain (e.g., NMFS.LOCAL), and click 🔄 Load OUs.
  3. Check one or more Organizational Units (and keep ☑️ Include Subtree (Sub-OUs) checked if desired), then click ✔ Add Checked Container(s).
  4. Click Sync Now to import computer accounts and automatically start background probing.

Non-Blocking Background Batched Probing & Logon User Detection

  • Clicking 📡 Probe (or letting the automatic background timer run) probes computers in parallel batches via a dedicated background RunspacePool so the WPF UI remains 100% responsive with zero freezing.
  • Multi-Tier Logon User Resolution: For every online host, PSDeploy resolves the logged-on user via:
    1. Tier 1 (WinRM CIM): Queries Win32_ComputerSystem.UserName, active explorer.exe process owners, and quser.exe output.
    2. Tier 2 (DCOM Fallback): Falls back to DCOM WMI if WinRM is restricted.
    3. Tier 3 (SMB quser /server:HOST): Queries Terminal Services / Remote RPC over port 445.
    4. Tier 4 (Remote Registry): Reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Authentication\LogonUI\LastLoggedOnUser when interactive session queries are blocked.

7. Running Deployments & Live Step Diagnostic Details

To deploy a package to one or more target computers:

  1. Check the Deploy checkbox next to one or more target computers in the Computer Inventory grid.
  2. Select the desired package in the Package Library tree (verify its name appears in the green Active Package badge inside the 🚀 DEPLOYMENT panel).
  3. Click 🚀 Deploy Selected Package.

Each deployment runs asynchronously in the background. Selecting a task in the Running Deployments & Deployment History table filters the bottom Status Log to show all target computers for that deployment run.

Inspecting Live File Staging Progress & Step Diagnostic Output

Double-click any row in the Status Log to open the Deployment Details modal window for that target computer. All file transfers run silently in the background (with zero OS copy popups) and report live file-by-file staging percentages and real-time standard output directly inside the Details Preview and Step Output & Diagnostic Details panes:

8. Status Log Filtering & Exporting Reports (💾 Export to CSV)

  • Per-Column Filtering & Sorting: Type into any filter box in the Status Log header (Computer Name, Package, Current / Last Step, Status, Start Time, End Time, Total Duration, Details) or click the ▾ dropdown button on any column header for Excel-style distinct value filtering.
  • 💾 Export to CSV — Exports the status log rows (including timestamp, computer name, package name, step progress, status, duration, and full diagnostic details) to a standard UTF-8 CSV file for compliance reporting and auditing.
  • 🗑 Delete Row / 🧹 Clear Status — Removes selected or all completed log entries from the current view.
  • ⏹ Stop Deployment — Signals all active background deployment runspaces to halt after their current operation.

9. Common Installer Exit Codes & Troubleshooting Reference

Exit Code Source / Installer Type Meaning & PSDeploy Handling
0 All Installers / Scripts Success: Command or installer completed normally with no errors.
1641 Windows Installer (msiexec) Success (Reboot Initiated): The installer completed successfully and initiated a system restart. Treated as Success by default.
3010 Windows Installer / Setup.exe Success (Reboot Required): The installation succeeded, and a reboot is required to complete changes. Treated as Success by default.
2359302 Windows Update Standalone (wusa.exe / .msu) Success (Already Installed): The update is already installed on the target system. Treated as Success by default.
17003 Microsoft Office Click-to-Run (setup.exe /configure) Success (Click-to-Run Uninstall / Reconfiguration Finalized): Returned by Office Click-to-Run bootstrapper during silent removal (e.g., RemoveAll.xml). PSDeploy waits for OfficeClickToRun.exe removal tasks to settle and marks the step as Success.
1603 Windows Installer (msiexec) Fatal Error During Installation: Check if another MSI install is in progress, if prerequisites are missing, or inspect the step's diagnostic output in the Deployment Details modal.
1618 Windows Installer (msiexec) Another Installation Already in Progress: Wait for the existing msiexec.exe process on the target host to complete and redeploy.
